newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court denies Abrams Iran-Contra appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court denies Abrams Iran-Contra appeal.

text.p: The Supreme Court Friday rejected an appeal by former Reagan State Department official Elliott Abrams over his censure for his role in the Iran-Contra scandal in the mid-1980s.

The justices let stand a ruling by the Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia that Abrams, a former assistant secretary of state for inter-American affairs, could be disciplined despite a 1992 pardon from President George Bush.

Abrams pleaded guilty in 1991 to two misdemeanor counts of withholding information from Congress in 1986 when it was investigating the Reagan White House scheme to sell arms to Iran secretly and divert the profits to the Nicaraguan rebels.

The District of Columbia bar association's Board of Professional Responsibility proposed a one-year suspension for Abrams, but the appeals court said he only should be censured. In his appeal, his lawyers argued the presidential pardon bars the appeals court from imposing any disciplinary sanctions.
But the Supreme Court denied the appeal without comment or dissent. Abrams, a lawyer, has not practiced law since 1980. He heads a conservative think tank.
